__comment: Trade Counter â€” the room-anchor furniture piece that designates a sealed room as a Shop.
This is the first furniture definition in the game. Its schema establishes the pattern
for all future furniture items.
ROOM DESIGNATION:
A sealed room (enclosed walls + one or more doors) containing a Trade Counter
is automatically designated as a 'shop' room. The room type is re-evaluated
whenever any furniture is added to or removed from the room.
Only one Trade Counter per room is valid. A second counter invalidates the room
designation until one is removed.
ROOM VALIDATION:
A shop room may only contain items whose furniture_category is listed in
room_compatible_categories. If any item with a category in
room_invalidating_categories is placed inside the room, the Shop designation
is immediately removed. The room reverts to an undesignated room until the
offending item is removed.
See furniture_category field on each furniture item for its category string.
SELL SIDE (automated):
All items stored in room_compatible storage units inside the shop room are
automatically available for sale when a merchant visits. The merchant checks
each item against their want list and buys matching stock at
base_trade_value Â± demand_modifier. The colony receives gold coins equal to
the transaction total. Sold items are removed from shop storage immediately.
BUY ORDERS (player-configured, automated):
The player configures buy orders on the Trade Counter via the UI.
Schema per order: { item_id, max_count, max_price_per_unit }
When a merchant carries an item matching a buy order:
- The colony buys as many units as available up to max_count.
- If gold coin balance is insufficient for the full order, partial fill applies:
buy as many units as coins allow at the stated price.
- Purchased goods are placed in available shop room storage first.
If shop storage is full, goods are dropped on the shop floor.
- Dwarves then haul floor goods to appropriate colony stockpiles.
Buy orders persist indefinitely and re-evaluate on every merchant visit.
Default: empty array (no buy orders). Configured per save, not in this file.
COIN FLOW:
Net coins = coins received from sales âˆ’ coins spent on buy orders.
If net is positive, gold coins are added to the nearest stockpile_currency stockpile
or dropped at the Trade Counter if none exists.
If net is negative (buy orders exceed sale revenue in a single visit),
the deficit is drawn from the colony's existing coin stockpile.
If the colony cannot cover the deficit, buy orders are partially filled
until coins run out.
MERCHANT VISIT CONDITION:
Merchants will only stop at the colony if a valid shop room exists AND the
shop has at least one item in storage OR at least one active buy order.
A shop room with a Trade Counter but no stock and no buy orders is treated
as inactive â€” caravans pass by without stopping.
TRADE NOTIFICATION:
On trade completion a summary toast is posted:
'Trade complete â€” sold X items, bought Y items, net +Z coins.'
Full transaction log is accessible from the Trade Counter inspect panel.
trade_definition.description: A heavy stone slab counter. Marks the room as an active shop and manages all trade with visiting merchants.
__comment_collision: collision_regions defines one or more axis-aligned boxes in furniture-local block coordinates.
Origin (0,0,0) = bottom-front-left corner of the footprint. Y is up. Units are game blocks (0.5 m).
Each region is read by the furniture placement system to create CollisionShape3D nodes at runtime.
Multi-region is used when different parts of the piece have different heights (e.g. beds).
A single region covering the full footprint at the correct visual height is the common case.

__comment: Item entity definitions for all dropped / harvested resources.
Loaded on demand when an item is spawned â€” NOT held in memory at boot.
Fields:
display_name  â€” human-readable name shown in UI and tooltips
description   â€” one-sentence flavour text shown in the inspect panel
model         â€” path to the MagicaVoxel .glb micro-voxel model (res:// path)
stack_max     â€” container capacity unit (integer â‰¥ 1). Ground stockpile zones store
ONE item per tile (SH parity, Alen 2026-07-06); stack_max applies to
the future container path (barrel/chest/shelf).
weight_class  â€” 'light' | 'heavy' â€” affects dwarf haul speed
light: full haul speed; heavy: Ã—0.7 haul speed while any heavy item
is in the pouch (the pouch carries anything â€” SH parity, Alen 2026-07-06)
base_trade_value â€” base Trade Point (TP) value used by the trade session UI
actual price fluctuates Â±20% based on caravan demand model
material_tags â€” flat string array; must include at least one 'stockpile_*' tag
used by stockpile zone filters and crafting ingredient queries

__comment: Storage Barrel - the first functional storage container (doc 19).
Follows the trade_counter.json schema. NEW fields established by doc 19:
item_key   - the resources.json ITEM form a dwarf fetches to install this piece
placement  - 'floor' | 'floor_wall' (floor_wall = needs a solid block behind the back face)
yaw_steps  - placement-ghost rotation steps (R key, 90 degrees each)

SH parity 2026-07-11; render_contents false = opaque density container)
barrel.json.description: A stout oak barrel bound in iron. Holds a small stock of whatever the colony hauls into it.

__comment: Bench - cheap mass seating for the tavern hall (doc 21, doc 62 candidate list).
Follows the doc 19 placement schema (item_key/placement/yaw_steps). Plain
placeable furniture, no room_anchor, no storage. Seating/sit-down behaviour
depends on the dwarf needs/mood system (doc 41), which is not yet implemented -
this piece is scenery for now, exactly like the shelf and chest were scenery
before doc 19 Phase 3 wired up hauling.
bench.json.description: A long dwarven bench, thick-legged and built to outlast whoever sits on it.

__comment: Door - the doc 22 prerequisite for doc 34's sealed-room detection.
RESIZED 2026-08-06 (Alen playtest feedback): footprint is 2x1 (was 1x1),
visually 2 blocks wide x 4 blocks tall - the original single-tile slab
read as out-of-proportion next to 3-tall dwarves and 1-wide corridors.
Both footprint cells matter for sealing: RoomManager now registers EVERY
footprint cell a door occupies as a sealing boundary (not just the
origin cell), so a 2-wide door only seals a room if BOTH tiles stop the
flood-fill - see FurniturePlacementController._install/_teardown_installed
passing component.cells (the full footprint) to on_furniture_changed(),
and RoomManager.on_furniture_changed()'s updated 'cells: Array[Vector3i]'
signature.
COLLISION_REGIONS IS DELIBERATELY EMPTY. Every other furniture piece uses
collision_regions to register NavGrid-blocking occupancy (see
FurniturePlacementController._install). A door must stay walkable, so it
carries no occupancy boxes at all - placing one changes nothing about
pathing. It IS still footprint-tracked (blocks a stockpile zone from being
drawn on the same tile, which you wouldn't want anyway) and IS tracked by
RoomManager as a sealing boundary via the direct on_furniture_changed()
call FurniturePlacementController makes on install/uninstall.
Per doc 34: 'Dwarves always close doors behind them. Door blocks are
always treated as sealed for temperature calculation purposes regardless
of animation state.' v1 has no open/close animation at all - every
installed door is permanently 'closed' for sealing purposes, which is a
strict superset of that rule (always-sealed is always at least as sealed
as 'sealed except when a dwarf is mid-walk-through').
PLACEMENT: v1 has no doorway validation (no check that the door sits
between two solid walls) - only the standard NavGrid.is_walkable(cell)
check every floor piece gets. Place doors sensibly; a door in the open
does nothing (RoomManager's flood-fill will simply fail to find a
bounded interior on either side of it).
door.json.description: A stout double plank door on iron hinges. Dwarves pass through freely; it seals the room for warmth.

__comment: Hearth â€” redesigned 2x2 stone fire bowl (doc 30, 2026-10-01).
Authored at 8 voxels per block, 0.125 export scale baked into the GLB.
Stone rim is 1 block high; tallest flame is 2 blocks. Placement and collision cover 2x2x2.
RoomManager reads heat_source.heat_units. A multi-cell hearth contributes 400 units once, at its origin.
The mesh has static flame geometry; light emission and animation are separate features.
The shared packed-furniture item and floor-placement behavior are unchanged.
hearth.json.description: A broad bowl of dressed stone with an iron grate, glowing coals and rising flames.

__comment: Storage Chest - the density step up from the barrel (doc 19 container ladder:
barrel 8 -> chest 24 -> future vault-class). Schema notes: see barrel.json.
storage_chest.json.description: A heavy plank chest with iron-bound corners. Densest storage the colony can build today.

__comment: Storage Shelf - the WYSIWYG container (doc 19): contents render ON the shelf at the
anchor points below, capacity == anchor count (never hold more than is visible).
GROUND SHELF (Alen, 2026-07-11): placement is plain 'floor' - no wall requirement.
The model is slated for hand-authoring by Alen (symmetric from all angles, no back
panel); the generator's version is interim. anchors are furniture-local block coords
(origin = bottom-front-left, same convention as collision_regions); anchor_scale is
the stored item render scale - 0.5 per SH ATTITEM parity (2026-07-11), tune-by-eye dial.
storage_shelf.json.description: Two stout plank shelves on heavy oak uprights. Everything stored on it stays in plain sight.

__comment: Tavern Bar - the room-anchor for a Tavern room (doc 21, doc 51, doc 62).
Follows the trade_counter.json room-anchor pattern PLUS the doc 19 placement
fields (item_key/placement/yaw_steps), so unlike trade_counter this piece is
actually placeable via the Build panel today.
STATUS (doc 21, 2026-08-03): room_anchor / room_type / room_compatible_categories /
room_invalidating_categories / max_per_room are DATA ONLY right now, exactly like
trade_counter's copy of these fields - no script reads them yet (verified: no
'room_type' or 'RoomData' reference anywhere in scripts/ as of this doc). Tavern
room detection, traveler serving, and ale consumption (doc 51) are a separate,
unbuilt system. Placing this piece today gets you a real, fetchable, installable
counter with no gameplay behaviour attached - the room-anchor fields simply mean
the future room-detection system (whenever it lands, likely alongside doc 34's
sealed-room flood-fill) does not need this file touched again.
MATERIAL: wood, not stone - unlike trade_counter (grandfathered pre-material-rule,
doc 62 categorises it as an industrial anchor). The bar is a piece dwarves USE
socially, so it follows the 2026-07-11 furniture-is-woodwork rule. This also keeps
it visually distinct from the stone Trade Counter at a glance.
tavern_bar.json.description: A long oak counter with iron tap fittings. The heart of the tavern hall.
